He found the end zone twice, including a late pass to Xavier Hutchinson with under a minute remaining. But there never was a moment where he felt like it just click. In fact, everything felt difficult. Stroud finished with a season-low 153 passing yards. He had one throw of over 30 yards, coming to Tank Dell in the second quarter. That pass, despite Dell's comments postgame, probably wasn't even going to him and it was an overthrown ball intended for Jaylin Noel. And in overtime, Stroud threw a pass into coverage that was initially intercepted before being dropped. Stroud wasn't the reason Houston lost. He also wasn't the reason Houston could find a pulse in the second half. item.title: Borussia Dortmund vs. Werder Bremen DFB-Pokal preview: Team news and predicted lineups
item.description: Borussia Dortmund vs. Werder Bremen DFB-Pokal preview: Team news and predicted lineups Borussia Dortmund host Werder Bremen for the second time this month as the two sides lock horns in the second round of the DFB-Pokal on Tuesday. BVB Dortmund will hope to continue their momentum with a third successive win in three competitions. After they got back to winning ways in Europe with Serhou Guirassy's brace in Baku, Niko Kovac's side relied on a late winner by Maximilian Beier against Eintracht Frankfurt. In a week that will end with the “Der Klassiker” at FC Bayern, Dortmund could take a huge step in both domestic competitions. A DFB-Pokal winner with both Eintracht Frankfurt and Bayern, Kovac has failed to get past the Round of 16 stage in his last three attempts with Wolfsburg and Dortmund. Bremen The six-time cup winners started the Bundesliga campaign with a heavy defeat against Europa League finalists Freiburg. However, their only defeat since then came in a 7-0 friendly loss to Twente during the international break. With Niclas Füllkrug in fine form, Daniel Thioune's men could even push for European return. The Green and Whites were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal by Arminia Bielefeld in the last two seasons. Head-to-head Füllkrug's two penalty-kicks in Mainz meant the former BVB striker leads the Torjägerkanone race all by himself with eight goals. The former Germany international scored the injury-time equalizer against Dortmund as Bremen came from two-goal down to earn a dramatic point after the international break. Bremen prevailed in the last three cup encounters against Dortmund, with all of those ties coming at the Round of 16 stage. The winners on Tuesday will earn a place in the last 16 of this season's competition. Team News Kovac confirmed Konstantinos Karetsas will remain on the sidelines as his pre-match press conference also hinted at the absence of the Greece international for the Bayern clash as well. Ramy Bensebaini will serve the second and last game of suspension for his red card in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. Olivier Deman is a doubt for the visitors after he had to be substituted off at half-time against Mainz. Despite Bremen's long injury list – including star players Jens Stage, Justin Njinmah and Niklas Stark – Thioune could still decide to rest the likes of Karl Hein and Füllkrug. Predicted Lineups BVB: Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck ©; Ryerson, Veerman, Svensson; Chukwuemeka, Bellingham; Guirassy, Fabio Silva Bremen: Hein; Arthur, Pieper, Friedl ©, Deman; Reis, Lynen; Chuki; Dinkci, Grüll; Füllkrug

item.description: Brazil win North Zone group in CONMEBOL Futsal Evolution League Brazil, represented by its senior and U-20 national teams, won the 2026 CONMEBOL Futsal Evolution League Credits: CONMEBOL Brazil, represented by its U-20 and senior national teams, won the North Zone group of the CONMEBOL Futsal Evolution League. In Sunday's (25) two matches against Venezuela, the U-20s cruised to a 5-0 win, while the senior team won 3-2. The results took Brazil to 17 points in the competition, level with Colombia. However, the Seleção claimed top spot on tiebreakers. Venezuela earned 11 points, Peru eight and Ecuador two. The title qualified Brazil for the CONMEBOL Futsal Evolution League final, where it will face Argentina, winner of the South Zone group. The final will take place in 2027. __instagram:https://www.instagram.com/p/De7ywhVCkMz/__ In the tournament, each country is represented by its U-20 and senior national teams. Results from both age groups counted toward the points tally used to determine the champion. Each win was worth three points and each draw one. In the 2026 CONMEBOL Futsal Evolution League, Brazil's senior team lost 3-2 to Colombia, drew 4-4 with Peru, thrashed Ecuador 7-0 and beat Venezuela 3-2. The U-20 team beat Colombia 3-2, drew 3-3 with Peru, defeated Ecuador 4-1 and cruised past Venezuela 5-0. The North Zone group of the CONMEBOL Futsal Evolution League was held at the Ivo Sguissardi Sports Hall in Xanxerê, Santa Catarina. __instagram:https://www.instagram.com/p/De7vYuYFuH8/?img_index=1__ This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. NFL: Dallas Cowboys (-4.5, 44.5) at Philadelphia Eagles Russell: The Cowboys' offense is overrated. After a respectable start, when adjusting for garbage time and high-leverage plays like turnovers and fourth downs, the Cowboys have been tumbling down the rankings of advanced metrics like weighted EPA/Play and Success Rate. It hasn't helped that they've faced top-five units in the Buccaneers and Packers, but their early season numbers were propped up by facing teams outside of the top 10. Plus, if you apply time for teams' scouting what Dallas wants to do, you can see why the Cowboys can't just rely on "out-talenting" the opponent. Few defensive coordinators are more familiar with Dallas than Vic Fangio, and the Eagles have been better at limiting opponents' EPA/Play (a metric that's augmented by the explosiveness that the Cowboys live and die by) than they have with raw Success Rate. It was a one-game sample size, but Tanner McKee's first start of the season in relief of Hurts went about as you might expect, as the Eagles were 26th (of 28) in the metrics above. On a positive note, McKee didn't turn the ball over, despite 45 pass attempts against the Panthers. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have already been ruled out for Monday, which won't help Philadelphia's potential for chunk yardage. However, the possible return of Saquon Barkley alters what might be asked of McKee, and makes it only more likely that the Eagles will be able to sustain long, clock-chewing drives between the 20s, against a Cowboys defense that's been known to give them up. With neither team compelled to put the football at risk, and the familiarity with what to expect from the opposing offense, we should expect a similar game to when the Eagles were on the other side of this scenario — a score with a combined total in mid-to-high 30s like that night in Chicago. Plus, if you apply time for teams' scouting what Dallas wants to do, you can see why the Cowboys can't just rely on "out-talenting" the opponent. Few defensive coordinators are more familiar with Dallas than Vic Fangio, and the Eagles have been better at limiting opponents' EPA/Play (a metric that's augmented by the explosiveness that the Cowboys live and die by) than they have with raw Success Rate. It was a one-game sample size, but Tanner McKee's first start of the season in relief of Hurts went about as you might expect, as the Eagles were 26th (of 28) in the metrics above. On a positive note, McKee didn't turn the ball over, despite 45 pass attempts against the Panthers. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have already been ruled out for Monday, which won't help Philadelphia's potential for chunk yardage. However, the possible return of Saquon Barkley alters what might be asked of McKee, and makes it only more likely that the Eagles will be able to sustain long, clock-chewing drives between the 20s, against a Cowboys defense that's been known to give them up. With neither team compelled to put the football at risk, and the familiarity with what to expect from the opposing offense, we should expect a similar game to when the Eagles were on the other side of this scenario — a score with a combined total in mid-to-high 30s like that night in Chicago. item.title: Eagles’ Landon Dickerson takes to IG to tease MNF injury return vs. Cowboys
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Eagles’ Landon Dickerson takes to IG to tease MNF injury return vs. Cowboys appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With their season spiraling, the Philadelphia Eagles received much-needed relief as Landon Dickerson is set to return from his knee injury. Dickerson was a full participant in practice on Saturday and was listed as questionable ahead of the Eagles’ matchup against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday Night Football. He has not played since Philadelphia’s season-opener against the Washington Commanders. On Monday, the 28-year-old offensive guard took to Instagram to tease his return , posting a series of pictures of himself. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Let’s go! 🦅,” wrote Dickerson in the caption. View this post on Instagram Fans were fired up for the three-time Pro Bowler. “We’ve missed you, Landon! Glad you’re back! Go Birds! 💚🦅,” said @kallie.fiorito. “Can’t wait, brother!” added @michael____philly_nation. “Welcome back, Landon 🙌🏽. We believe in you, Big Country 💚,” stated @labellagitana85. “I CHOOSE VIOLENCE TOMORROW, @landondickerson69 💪🏽💪🏽💪🏽💪🏽🫡🫡🫡🫡🦅🦅🦅🦅,” commented @eaglesdadx3. “Knew you were gonna go out better than that 💪🏾💯🫡,” quipped @uptown_larry. Dickerson’s return should be a morale booster for the Eagles, who have lost Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season due to blood clots in his lungs. Saquon Barkley, meanwhile, has missed the last two weeks due to a hamstring injury. Philadelphia is amid a four-game losing skid. Dickerson was placed on the back burner in September after trying to play through his knee injury in Week 1. In a report from ESPN’s Tim McManus, Dickerson admitted that it was a hasty decision. He will instantly shore up the offensive line, which should bode well for Tanner McKee. item.title: Man United’s problems are much bigger than Michael Carrick – and much harder to fix
item.description: There was a time, not too long ago, when Michael Carrick was the answer for Manchester United . He seemed to have the answers, too. Now he is stumped in his search for them. “Certainly, to get to this point, is there’s a lot of questions to find the answers to,” he said. And this point may be the end point : 16th in the Premier League , 20th in the Champions League, eight games without a win after back-to-back thrashings at the hands of small clubs. Carrick, who had the best record in the Premier League last season after his January appointment, stands on the brink of the sack. Carrick’s regime has crumbled at startling speed, with brutal cruelty to a fundamentally decent man with a genuine affection for the club. It is part of a cycle at United, whirring around ever quicker as managers come and go. Carrick has been unable to stop history repeating itself at Old Trafford. He has been left wondering why. “If I really had the answer, I wouldn’t have let it happen,” he said. “If I could do something about it and there was something that I could really control, then I wouldn’t have. I’ve tried to do everything I can to not be in this position.” Michael Carrick is on the brink of the sack (Martin Rickett/PA) A few months ago, Carrick was the manager who came in with the clarity of thought to find a formation straight away, the credibility and personality to get the support of his players, the decisiveness to make a series of successful substitutions. He has been left wondering why. “If I really had the answer, I wouldn’t have let it happen,” he said. “If I could do something about it and there was something that I could really control, then I wouldn’t have. I’ve tried to do everything I can to not be in this position.” Michael Carrick is on the brink of the sack (Martin Rickett/PA) A few months ago, Carrick was the manager who came in with the clarity of thought to find a formation straight away, the credibility and personality to get the support of his players, the decisiveness to make a series of successful substitutions. Now? He lost to Bournemouth using Ruben Amorim’s system and with the armband worn by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s chosen captain, Harry Maguire. The skipper who won Footballer of the Year after the initial, dramatic improvement under Carrick, Bruno Fernandes, was dropped after criticising the manager’s tactics , and left unused on the bench as a misfit, Joshua Zirkzee, and a teenager, Shea Lacey, came on ahead of him. A relationship feels fractured; perhaps not turning to Fernandes was a sign Carrick realised he had reached the end. The Portuguese has been by far United’s best player since Sir Alex Ferguson retired, but he lost form towards the end of Erik ten Hag’s reign. The accusation is that too many United footballers help get managers the sack. Carrick could join the list of the dismissed. Bruno Fernandes stayed on the bench against Bournemouth (PA Wire) He has not had the answer to his players’ underachievement. The list of those who have had poor seasons so far includes virtually everyone: Fernandes and Maguire, but also Senne Lammens, Diogo Dalot, Lisandro Martinez, Ayden Heaven, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Matheus Cunha. Nor has Carrick had answers as to their lack of mobility. Too few can run far enough or fast enough, and if that suggests pre-season has not left them fit enough, the fault may lie with those who built this slow squad. The Amorim-esque 3-4-3 Carrick used against Bournemouth seemed designed to camouflage the inability of too many players in central positions to cover much distance. Defensively, he has had few answers. United have conceded early goals in Europe and late ones in England. They have conceded from set-pieces and individual errors. They have conceded to 10 men. They have conceded two goals in swift succession on multiple occasions. United have been defensively dismal and that will likely cost Carrick (Reuters) And if much of that suggests they have had insufficient resilience, United arguably have not had enough mental or physical strength. Carrick’s style of management is to try and give his players confidence, to back them. He has not been rewarded. When he required a performance, twice in five days they delivered a surrender. Too often Carrick, who showed such a sure touch with his selections last season, has seemed to pick the wrong team. It has been altogether harder to work out what the right side would be: sporting director Jason Wilcox left him short-staffed in some positions and short of quality in others. Martinez would agree ... Cunha floundered as a centre-forward, but the only specialists are the injury-prone Benjamin Sesko and the inadequate Zirkzee. Only one player’s preferred position is left-back: the injury-prone and currently-injured Luke Shaw. Four others have had to operate there, none with conspicuous success. Carlos Baleba has floundered after a promising start (AP) Then there is the midfield, the area Carrick used to patrol. His only partnership to work was Casemiro and Kobbie Mainoo, one gone, the other now sidelined. Wilcox’s £155m overhaul was supposed to alter that. Carlos Baleba at least began well but, like many a United signing, has since seemed to regress alarmingly. Tielemans seems unable to operate in a midfield duo and Carrick has shunted him further forward. It is an accurate reflection of Santos’s mediocrity that he has started six matches and United have lost five of them. Perhaps Carrick, whose time at Middlesbrough began promisingly and then tailed off, is a manager who runs out of answers. There was at least a meritocratic element to his appointment at Old Trafford, after taking 39 points from 17 games in interim charge. Picking Carrick as caretaker was a rare thing Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada have got right. Sacking him, two months into a season, will underline their otherwise wretched record. Because if Carrick does not have the answers to fix United, there is no indication they do either.

item.title: Brewers Pitcher Trashes Tropicana Field Ahead Of Game 3 Against Rays
item.description: Tropicana Field The Milwaukee Brewers held a workout at Tropicana Field on Sunday, and part of that workout was practicing catching pop-ups. Big leaguers don't really need to work on catching pop-ups often, but Tropicana Field presents a unique challenge. The color of the roof makes it challenging to find the ball, so the Brewers, like other teams, are spending extra time getting used to their environment. "Whoever decided to make the roof the same (expletive) color as the baseball is a (expletive) idiot,” Brewers closer Trevor Megill reportedly said while walking by reporters on Sunday, per WISN 12 News' Dario Melendez. Megill has never held back while talking to reporters and usually says exactly what he's thinking. He has been great for the Brewers in the postseason and all year, really, but he knows the challenge the roof presents to the defense behind him. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! The roof at Tropicana Field also has unique rules when it comes to the catwalks, which also add to the adventure of catching balls hit high. Per the official ground rules, a "batted ball that strikes either of the lower two catwalks (known as the 'C-Ring' and the 'D-Ring'), including any lights or suspended objects attached to either of those catwalks as well as any angled support rods that connect the 'C-Ring' to the masts that support the 'D-Ring' in fair territory" is a home run. However, a "batted ball that strikes either of the upper catwalks (known as the 'A-Ring' and the 'B-Ring'), including the masts that support each of those catwalks as well as any angled support rods that connect the 'B-Ring' to the masts that support the 'C-Ring' in fair territory" is in play. The Rays also have to deal with the roof, but they have much more practice with it. For the Brewers, it's another challenge they have to deal with as they look to go up 3-0. item.title: McKenna signs Brisbane Lions contract extension
item.description: McKenna helped Brisbane Lions win their third straight Premiership in 2026 [Getty Images] Tyrone's Conor McKenna has signed a two-year contract extension with Australian Football League side Brisbane Lions. The 30-year-old half-back joined the Lions in 2023 and helped the Queensland side win the Premiership title in 2024 and 2026. The Eglish native previously had a five-year spell with Essendon before returning home to help Tyrone win the All-Ireland SFC title in 2021. This year, McKenna helped the Lions clinch a third straight Premiership title with victory over the Fremantle Dockers in the AFL Grand Final at Melbourne Cricket Ground. The Lions have also signed Lincoln McCarthy and ruckman Darcy Fort. "It is fantastic to have Darcy, Conor and Linc committed to the Brisbane Lions as they have all played an important role in our success and will continue to do so," said Lions general manager Danny Daly. "All three offer plenty on field as players, and their experience and leadership are also incredibly valuable - especially in supporting our younger players. "We look forward to having all three players and their families continue to be part of the Brisbane Lions."

His form was fragile, highlighted by an 80 on Friday at The Masters that left him 12-over par after two rounds. He also lost two of three matches at the WGC-Matchplay, finishing at the bottom of his group. Despite these struggles, he told the media he felt ready to compete again. Optimism Meets Reality on the Course DeChambeau expressed hope ahead of the first round, stating, “I’m actually excited. It’s been a long time coming.” He went further, telling reporters, “Look, do I know I can finish out the week? Yeah. Do I know that I can contend? Yes. Do I know that I can finally enjoy golf again? Yes. That’s a big step for me and my health and my mental state.” That confidence vanished quickly on the course. According to Yardbarker , the golfer got off to a poor start by posting a score of 76 on Thursday. The gap between his mental readiness and his physical execution was stark. Golf Digest reported he admitted his game was far from optimal, stating, “My golf swing is a wreck,” he said. The contrast between his public statements and his performance defined the week. Despite the bad score, he tried to find a silver lining in the emotional return to competition. He noted that while he hated the golf, the emotional side of being back in a competitive environment was positive. However, the tournament did not serve as the launchpad he needed. It stands as the final chapter of his PGA Tour career, ending not with a victory or a strong finish, but with a struggle that foreshadowed his eventual departure. The Financial and Strategic Shift Ahead The events at the Memorial set the stage for a massive shift in DeChambeau’s career trajectory. His contract situation with LIV Golf has become complex, with a bankruptcy judge recently rejecting 19 LIV contracts, including DeChambeau’s. According to Yardbarker, LIV still owes him $5.77 million based on their filings. ESPN reported that he “remains committed to LIV Golf” and is working behind the scenes toward a new version of the league. Speculation about his financial future has grown alongside these legal filings. Charlie Stebbings and Charlie Methven explored on the October 25 Business of Sport podcast if DeChambeau might gain from BC Partners’ suggested $300 million LIV investment. DeChambeau had previously been clear about his stance on leaving the PGA Tour. “For me, I personally don’t think that at this point in time I’m in a place in my career where I can risk things like that,” he said during the Memorial. That sentiment contrasts sharply with the current landscape where he is deeply involved in LIV 2.0 planning. The hosts on the podcast claimed that “all the serious golfers other than Bryson are out,” though this remains their opinion rather than a confirmed roster list. What the Future Holds for the Golfer The path forward for DeChambeau involves navigating a league in flux. With players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton having left, and others like Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith yet to confirm their status for LIV 2.0, the roster remains uncertain. The Business of Sport podcast suggested the new iteration could include a mix of experienced players and journeymen alongside DeChambeau. BC Partners’ connection to DeChambeau’s agency, GSE Worldwide, adds another layer to the story. The firm invested in GSE in 2024, and a spokesperson told Front Office Sports that BC Partners acts as a lender. However, the financial details were not made public, and GSE declined to say if DeChambeau is personally involved in those specific talks. This opacity continues to fuel questions about where the money flows and who benefits most from the league’s restructuring. DeChambeau’s future remains tied to the success of LIV 2.0. While he is one of the few players yet to confirm his plans for 2027, the league faces an uncertain future as more players announce departures. The question of whether he will return to the PGA Tour or the DP World Tour remains open, but his commitment to the Saudi-backed league appears firm despite the legal and financial hurdles.

item.title: Former Gunner takes credit for Xabi Alonso’s greatest managerial success
item.description: Former Gunner takes credit for Xabi Alonso’s greatest managerial success Granit Xhaka suggested last month that his tactical suggestion was a big factor in Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso’s success with Bayer Leverkusen. Photo by Ayush Kumar/Getty Images Given the cost to assemble Chelsea’s current squad and the reputation Xabi Alonso had when joining, the team’s start to the new season has been somewhat underwhelming. With no European football to distract them, Chelsea have won four, drawn one, and lost three of their opening eight Premier League fixtures. Most recently, they suffered a 2-0 defeat at home to a Tottenham Hotspur team who had scored six goals in their other seven league games. Alonso’s team have already slipped eight points off the pace, and even slow starters Liverpool look more likely to make a title challenge. Amid questions around Alonso’s tactics in Chelsea’s own fanbase, an interview from September has resurfaced in which former Gunner Granit Xhaka suggests the manager’s most famous team was inspired by him. Photo by George Wood/Getty Images “The first game when I went to Leverkusen with Xabi Alonso, we played Real Sociedad in Spain, the friendly game,” Xhaka recalled . “Xabi starts a back four, but the feeling on the pitch was not right. “I went to Xabi, I said, ‘Xabi, I think that this team, back four, we will struggle a lot’. He said, ‘why?’ I said, ‘I think that we don’t have this character [or] players for this back four’. And he changed. “This, for me, shows a big human being from a coach side. After this, everyone knows that we won the league unbeaten, we went to the Europa League final, we won the German cup after 32 years.” Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images Alonso obviously pushed to reunite with Xhaka over the summer, but Sunderland refused to sell amid suggestions that they viewed Chelsea’s first bid as insulting. Though there were reports at the time that Xhaka was open to the move, he has since told the media that he felt his job with the north-east club wasn’t done. Without Xhaka’s advice to fall back on, Alonso now needs to find his own strategy to turn things around at Chelsea. Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images

item.title: “Aren’t professional”: Gary Neville launches stunning tirade at Man United’s sorry players
item.description: “Aren’t professional”: Gary Neville launches stunning tirade at Man United’s sorry players In another chaotic weekend of action for Manchester United fans, their team was embarrassed at home by AFC Bournemouth. The game They were ripped apart 0-3 on a turgid afternoon for the club. Michael Carrick was given a warm reception from the Stretford End as he left the pitch and headed down the tunnel. Nonetheless, the players felt the tirade of anger as they were booed and jeered while they followed behind him. Gary Neville was also far from impressed by what he had just witnessed from United’s players. Neville’s comments Speaking on his podcast on Sky Sports , he laid into the standards at the club and focused his anger on a selection of players. He explained, “there’s a few of them that aren’t that professional. There’s a couple of them… I live in Manchester, they’re not that professional, some of them.” Elaborating further on their issues he claimed, “I’ve got no time for them. There’s a few of them that don’t go to bed at the right time. Don’t eat the right things. Don’t think about Manchester United every single minute of every single day.” Neville continued his outburst by asserting, “they are not living and breathing this football club, as they should be, like professionals should. And why? Why? Because it’s gone to their heads. But they still walk around like they’re King William… they’re not, they’re nothing.” The former United captain also referenced the banner in the Stretford End that is labelled “standards” and claimed that they left the club a long time ago. The pundit then defended his former teammate Carrick by stating he is a man with “integrity, credibility, decency, professionalism.” He finished his statements by claiming, “he’s not been able to get a tune out of them and they’ve turned on him. I know that because if Bruno’s turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they’re like behind the scenes.” Manchester United v Bournemouth Featured image by Dan Istitene via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Napoli confirm injuries to Badiashile and Spinazzola but get one defender back
item.description: Napoli confirm injuries to Badiashile and Spinazzola but get one defender back It has been a frustrating day for Napoli, who have recently learned that head coach Massimiliano Allegri will be suspended for the next two games, and are now preparing to go into Wednesday’s Serie A match against Monza without Benoit Badiashile or Leonardo Spinazzola, who are both injured. Napoli confirm injuries to Badiashile and Spinazzola, Rrahmani back The Lega Serie A confirmed on Monday that Allegri has been handed a two-match suspension after his outburst at the end of Napoli’s 3-3 draw against Roma on Saturday, which means he will have to sit out of Wednesday’s game against Monza and the return to his former club Juventus on Sunday. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Massimiliano Allegri, SSC Napoli head coach, reacts to his expulsion during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli have confirmed in a statement that they will be appealing the decision to hand Allegri a two-match suspension. The club has also confirmed in another statement that Badiashile and Spinazzola have suffered injuries after the 3-3 draw against Roma over the weekend. The bigger concern is for summer signing Badiashile, who has suffered a medium-grade strain to the rectus fermoris in his right leg, which is likely to keep him out of action for around a month according to initial reports from Gianluca Di Marzio . NAPLES, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Leonardo Spinazzola during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Bologna FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on September 13, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Spinazzola is facing a shorter period on the sidelines, but is still expected to miss the Monza game with a low-grade injury to the femoral biceps in his right thigh. The positive update is that Amir Rrahmani trained in full with the first-team group on Monday, which makes it a case of one in, two out in defence for Napoli.

item.title: Andre Onana: Champions League club poised to strike after Man United transfer green light
item.description: Andre Onana: Champions League club poised to strike after Man United transfer green light Manchester United may finally part company with André Onana on a permanent basis, according to recent reports. After two seasons at M16 in which he struggled for consistency, the Red Devils decided in the summer of 2025 to move on from the Cameroonian goalkeeper and sign a quality replacement. Senne Lammens arrived and became a massive hit, instantly elevating United’s goalkeeping department. Lammens ended Onana’s Old Trafford career Lammens’ arrival meant Onana’s exit, yet United could not secure a permanent departure in time. Instead, they struck a quick loan deal with Trabzonspor. Onana rediscovered his form in the Turkish Süper Lig, helping Trabzonspor finish third and reach the Europa League play-offs. Given how marvellous he had been, the Karadeniz Fırtınası were widely expected to sign him permanently. However, they failed to do so, with suggestions that they lacked the finances to complete the deal . They therefore requested another season-long loan, agreed to cover his wages, and United accepted. The Cameroonian has since picked up where he left off, dazzling between the sticks week after week. Consequently, there are now suggestions that Trabzonspor are looking to land him on a permanent basis. Galatasaray join the race for André Onana But while Trabzonspor dilly-dally, Africa Foot now claims that Galatasaray are looking to strike a quick deal with United for Onana. They report: “Galatasaray is showing strong interest in André Onana. The Turkish champions are ready to open negotiations with Manchester United to secure the services of the Cameroonian goalkeeper.” INEOS would welcome Galatasaray’s interest, as it could spark a bidding war with Trabzonspor and hand the Old Trafford chiefs a decent transfer fee for the keeper. item.title: Aston Martin Kept Wrenching on Stroll’s Car Past the Deadline. The FIA’s Answer Was the Pit Lane.
item.description: Photo: Sushrut Koche / Unsplash. Generic garage scene, not from the Austin race. Aston Martin worked on Lance Stroll’s car after the deadline, changed his suspension setup without sign-off, and swapped a stack of power unit parts under parc fermé. The stewards’ answer in Austin on Sunday: start the United States Grand Prix from the pit lane. The ruling is a clean example of how Formula 1’s 2026 parc fermé rules punish a team differently from an ordinary grid penalty. What the FIA has confirmed The ruling: Stewards’ Document 48 for the 2026 United States Grand Prix finds that Car 18, Stroll’s Aston Martin, must start the race from the pit lane. It was issued on Sunday, October 25, after the Technical Delegate’s report (Document 47). The breaches: the suspension setup was changed under parc fermé without approval, work on the car continued after the permitted deadline, and five power unit elements were replaced without the Technical Delegate’s approval. The rules cited: Articles B3.4.3a, B3.4.3b, B3.5.3 and B3.5.4, plus B8.2.2 with B8.2.3, of the FIA Formula 1 Regulations. The maths the stewards ran: each extra power unit element normally costs five grid places, so five elements would be 25 places. Article B3.5.3a, however, requires a pit lane start when parts are replaced under parc fermé without approval. The timing: the stewards say work continued more than two hours after qualifying ended and within five hours of the race formation lap. The route back: the document notes the right of appeal under Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code. Why a pit lane start is not just a bigger penalty Analysis from here. Stroll was provisionally 16th, so a 25-place drop would have sent him to the back of a 22-car grid anyway. What the pit lane start actually changes is the mechanism. A grid penalty is a cost teams budget for, and engine manufacturers routinely schedule parts changes around it. A parc fermé breach is a procedural offence, and the regulations remove the discount: no arithmetic, no slot on the grid, and release only after the field has left. That distinction matters for how Aston Martin plans its next set of parts. Taking penalties for new hardware is a normal trade. Doing it in the wrong window, without the Technical Delegate in the loop, converts a calculated cost into a rules violation. Aston Martin and Honda have already taken a grid penalty with an engine upgrade in Madrid , so the team knows the penalty route. Austin was a different route, and the one the regulations are designed to make unattractive. Photo: Nathanaël Desmeules / Unsplash. Generic circuit aerial, not Circuit of the Americas. item.content:encoded: Photo: Sushrut Koche / Unsplash. Generic garage scene, not from the Austin race. Aston Martin worked on Lance Stroll’s car after the deadline, changed his suspension setup without sign-off, and swapped a stack of power unit parts under parc fermé. The stewards’ answer in Austin on Sunday: start the United States Grand Prix from the pit lane. The ruling is a clean example of how Formula 1’s 2026 parc fermé rules punish a team differently from an ordinary grid penalty. What the FIA has confirmed The ruling: Stewards’ Document 48 for the 2026 United States Grand Prix finds that Car 18, Stroll’s Aston Martin, must start the race from the pit lane. It was issued on Sunday, October 25, after the Technical Delegate’s report (Document 47). The breaches: the suspension setup was changed under parc fermé without approval, work on the car continued after the permitted deadline, and five power unit elements were replaced without the Technical Delegate’s approval. The rules cited: Articles B3.4.3a, B3.4.3b, B3.5.3 and B3.5.4, plus B8.2.2 with B8.2.3, of the FIA Formula 1 Regulations. The maths the stewards ran: each extra power unit element normally costs five grid places, so five elements would be 25 places. Article B3.5.3a, however, requires a pit lane start when parts are replaced under parc fermé without approval. The timing: the stewards say work continued more than two hours after qualifying ended and within five hours of the race formation lap. The route back: the document notes the right of appeal under Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code. Why a pit lane start is not just a bigger penalty Analysis from here. Stroll was provisionally 16th, so a 25-place drop would have sent him to the back of a 22-car grid anyway. What the pit lane start actually changes is the mechanism. A grid penalty is a cost teams budget for, and engine manufacturers routinely schedule parts changes around it. A parc fermé breach is a procedural offence, and the regulations remove the discount: no arithmetic, no slot on the grid, and release only after the field has left. That distinction matters for how Aston Martin plans its next set of parts. Taking penalties for new hardware is a normal trade. Doing it in the wrong window, without the Technical Delegate in the loop, converts a calculated cost into a rules violation. Aston Martin and Honda have already taken a grid penalty with an engine upgrade in Madrid , so the team knows the penalty route. Austin was a different route, and the one the regulations are designed to make unattractive. Photo: Nathanaël Desmeules / Unsplash. Generic circuit aerial, not Circuit of the Americas. The competitive picture Everyone behind Stroll on the provisional grid moves up one place. That is a small gift to the midfield, and in a tight pack where one position can decide a point, small gifts count. For Aston Martin, the damage is a car starting last in traffic-free clean air, which helps tyre life and strategy flexibility but costs track position it will have to fight to recover. Teammate Fernando Alonso is unaffected by the ruling. There is also a season-long angle. Aston Martin has already committed to Alonso and Stroll for 2027 , and the car still has to find speed. A team chasing performance through late-weekend changes is a team under pressure, and the stewards just reminded it that pressure is not a defence. In a weekend where the front row historically decides the Austin race , the story at the other end of the grid was about process, not pace. What we do not know yet Why the work was done after the deadline. The stewards’ document records the breach, not Aston Martin’s motive. Whether Aston Martin will appeal. Nothing in the document says it will. How much the pit lane start cost on the day, which depends on the race itself, not the paperwork. Watch the next round for how Aston Martin sequences its power unit parts, and whether other teams quietly tighten their own parc fermé procedures after seeing how little room the stewards left themselves. item.description: After another wild week of the high school soccer season, it's time to look back on the best performances. Read about the players who stood out last week and let us know who you think should be the HSS North Jersey Player of the Week in the poll at the bottom of this page. Voting closes at 5 p.m. Thursday. Josh Santosh, Tenafly senior Santosh sent the Tigers to the Bergen County final for the first time since 2015 by scoring two goals, including the game-winner in a 3-2 victory over Ridgewood. Over three wins last week, he combined for five goals and two assists. Danny Scuro, Demarest junior Scuro pushed his team to its first Bergen County final since 1977 by picking up a 13-save shutout in a 2-0 win over top seed Bergen Catholic. He stopped 16 of 17 shots for the week. Adam Spadaccini, Lakeland junior Spadaccini came through with a Golden Goal in double overtime Saturday to give Lakeland its first Passaic County title since 1989. He finished with two goals in the win and totaled five goals and two assists on the week for the unbeaten Lancers. Max Zagorski, Becton junior Zagorski broke the Wildcats single-season scoring record last week with 32 goals, surpassing the previous mark of 29. He powered the offense with 12 goals in three wins. Madisyn Abella, Immaculate Heart junior Abella went on a tear last week with six goals and an assist over the Blue Eagles’ four wins. She scored a goal and set up another when they shut out Ridgewood in the Bergen County semifinal. Sydney Edwards, Bergen Tech sophomore Edwards struck for five more goals last week as Bergen Tech split two league matches. She completed the week with a team-high 23 goals, fourth most in Bergen County. Hope Ernst, Ramsey junior The Virginia commit kept Ramsey unbeaten by getting three goals and an assist in a 6-2 win over Old Tappan in the Bergen County semifinals . She tallied two goals earlier in the week against River Dell. The Manhattan commit tallied seven goals in three wins last week. VOTE! Note: If you can't see the poll, try refreshing the link or clearing the cache in your browser. item.title: Video: UFC fighter King Green live stream captures his own car accident in Los Angeles after the MMA veteran appeared to run a red light.
item.description: King Green just totaled his Range Rover. The UFC lightweight veteran was behind the wheel during a live stream and appeared to sail through a red light before colliding with another car on Hollywood Blvd. in Los Angeles. Fortunately, it looks as though nobody was hurt during the collision but there was significant damage to both vehicles. UFC fighter King Green totaled his custom Range Rover in a car accident on stream pic.twitter.com/jctc7ffgoO — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026 “We just got in a car accident, hopefully the people are okay,” Green said after the wreck. “That car is my baby too, it’s totaled. Why would she do that? I could see if I wasn’t paying attention or something like that, we were just driving all the way through. You can see her turn in front of us. At least we got the camera.” Green (36-18-1, 1 NC) is coming off a technical knockout loss to Esteban Ribovics at UFC 332 earlier this month in Salt Lake City, a defeat that snapped a four-fight win streak for the 40-year-old MMA veteran. No word yet on when Green plans to make his Octagon return, but first quarter 2027 seems likely. “Shit happens,” Green added.

item.title: NFL official addresses Green Bay Packers’ disputed calls after frustrating loss to Lions
item.description: The Green Bay Packers’ latest NFC North clash ended in disappointment, with Matt LaFleur’s men dropping a 20-17 decision to the Detroit Lions on Sunday in a game marred by mistakes from both sides. Much of the postgame discussion centered on the officials, whose controversial decisions at key points became a major source of frustration during the divisional showdown. Pool report with referee Alex Moore via reporter Ben Raven: pic.twitter.com/TUjTw028xv — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 26, 2026 ESPN reporter Rob Demovsky released the postgame pool report featuring questions for referee Alex Moore about the disputed decisions in the Packers’ loss. Moore addressed several of the controversial calls, but his explanations did little to ease the frustration surrounding the officiating. One of the first disputed decisions involved a third quarter unnecessary roughness flag against Devonte Wyatt. Uncertainty surrounded whether officials had already blown the whistle after Wyatt brought down Amon-Ra St. Brown. When the Lions receiver tried to keep moving, Wyatt made a second tackle, prompting the penalty. NFL official on disputed calls against the Green Bay Packers Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) sacks Green Bay Packers quarterback Love (10) during the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images “We ruled that the play was over. I can’t honestly hear if there was a whistle or not, but the tackler made the tackle, the play was over. Then, there was an additional action, and he basically tackled him again with force after the play was over,” Moore also explained the disputed intentional grounding call against Jordan Love late in the game. Although the Packers quarterback had moved outside the pocket before releasing the ball, his pass failed to reach the line of scrimmage, resulting in a costly penalty for Green Bay. Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) talks to center Cade Mays (64) before a play against Green Bay Packers during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Fans also drew comparisons to a Week 1 incident involving Lions quarterback Jared Goff, when a strip sack returned for a touchdown was overturned. They questioned how that ruling aligned with the intentional grounding call against Love. However, Green Bay must put the disappointing defeat behind it quickly, with the Packers set to host the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
